chapter: Taking New Orleans musicians on the road
title: Who went out first: Dodds, Carey and Gulf Coast players
summary: They sort out dates: Dodds and the others went in 1918 when the district closed; earlier they played the coast from Mobile to Laurel, Mississippi. Theaters' own pianists left to travel with them.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Oh, who went with you in 1914?
This is when we took Johnny Dodds and them around, but we didn't go directly to...
No, we didn't. We were taking Johnny Dodds and them in 1918.
19... When the district closed in New Orleans for the Army, you know...
They were going to take them to the Army. I do.
Do you remember? You know, Pete Lawless, they come around to the cabaret to get the... Mm-hmm. For them to sign up and all that. And so that's when they decided to go away. Yeah.
That was my... Well, what we wanted to say there in answer to Mr. Russell's question is that each theater had their own piano player and drummer. Yes. Some just a piano player.

And we got to meet all these fellas. Oh, yeah. And after we started our own show, why a lot of times when we needed a piano player, they'd leave. They'd leave any one of them to leave any house to go traveling, you see. And so...
I just wondered if any of the men from New Orleans had gone with you as early as 1914, before Mudcary and Dodds?
Yes, the Bay St. Louis. Just over the Bay St. Louis.
And up and down that coast from Mobile to New Orleans we played and up... coming up northward in Mississippi as far as Laurel, Mississippi. And then there. Yes.
Buddy Christian and Bud Scott. Yeah.
